Hi Samir / Rebecca —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery call (focus: SDK integration, auth, routing, structured output/tool-calling, embeddings + reranker, and observability hooks):

Summary of the call:
- Primary goal: embed low-latency assistant into customer support workflows and transactions while preserving traceability across FintechCo services.
- Key concerns: request tracing, request id propagation, per-token latency breakdowns in responses, and a clear dashboard for SLOs.
- Integration plan: SDK-based integration (Node or Python), backend-to-backend calls from FintechCo services into Redwood Dedicated; embeddings for semantic retrieval + small reranker for precision.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) Confirm tracing header preferences (W3C traceparent vs custom X- headers). We can support both, and will echo/propagate whichever you prefer.
2) Rishi to propose the exact header names we’ll emit for latency breakdowns (e.g., X-Redwood-Latency: tokens=12;model=34ms;queue=5ms) and sample log fields to index.
3) Technical workshop: 60-90m deep-dive with Solutions (Vivek + Rishi) to walk SDK setup (auth flow, routing policy, structured output/tool-calling examples). Please share 2 available slots next week.
4) Embeddings / reranker: draft recommendation and expected cost/latency trade-offs (Rishi to propose).
5) Share discovery notes + sample header file.

Attachments: 2026-03-01-fintechco-discovery-notes.pdf (call notes + initial MOP)

Open questions for you:
- Do you have a preferred trace header (traceparent / X-Request-Id / X-FT-ReqId)?
- Any retention or PI/PCI constraints for request-level logs we should be aware of?

I’ll loop in Vivek to schedule the workshop once you confirm preferred times and trace header.

Thanks Marissa — call was useful. A few clarifications from our side before the workshop: 

- Trace propagation: we standardize on W3C traceparent for distributed tracing across services. Can Redwood accept traceparent and also echo it in your logs/responses? We also use an internal header X-FT-ReqId (GUID) for customer-facing flows — would like that preserved end-to-end (request -> logs -> response).

- Latency breakdowns: we want to be able to attribute tail latency to queuing, model compute, and tokenization. What header(s) do you emit for that and will they be present on both hosted and dedicated deployments?

- Auth: we prefer service accounts with short-lived JWTs (OIDC/JWKS flow). Can you support that in Dedicated / Private?

- Embeddings & reranker: we plan to retrieve ~100 candidates initially from a vector store, then rerank top-20. Any guidance on cost/latency tradeoffs for that pattern?

If you can send a short tech note before the workshop that addresses these points, that’d be great. I can propose times for Wed/Thu next week.

Hi Samir — quick tech note addressing your questions. Happy to go deeper in the workshop.

1) Trace propagation
- We fully support W3C traceparent and will ingest that if provided. We also accept custom headers (e.g., X-FT-ReqId) and will echo them back in the response header so you can correlate client logs with Redwood logs.
- Recommendation: send traceparent + X-FT-ReqId. Redwood will: 1) attach trace context to internal spans, 2) include trace id in logs (field: trace.id), and 3) echo both headers back in the response.

2) Latency breakdown headers / logging fields
- Response header: X-Redwood-Latency (example): tokens=12;model=34ms;queue=5ms;network=2ms
- Response header: X-Redwood-Model-Version: gptx-1.2.3
- Log fields (JSON): trace.id, request.id (X-FT-ReqId), model.version, tokens.input, tokens.generated, latency.total_ms, latency.model_ms, latency.queue_ms. (We will provide a sample log mapping for ingestion into Splunk/Datadog.)
- These headers are available for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private; on Private we can also push logs to your Syslog/forwarder.

3) Auth / service accounts
- Supported: API keys (bearer), service-account JWTs via OAuth2 token exchange, and mTLS in Private deployments. We support JWKS for validating signed service account tokens. For Dedicated we recommend the short-lived JWT flow with a rotating key; we can provide a sample token exchange endpoint.

4) SDK setup & routing
- SDKs (Node/Python) include a top-level client that accepts: api_key OR jwt_token, region, and routing policy. Example (Node, illustrative):
  const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_API_KEY, region: 'us-west-2', routing: { tier: 'dedicated', fallback: 'hosted' } });
- SDKs auto-inject trace headers if you pass traceId in the request: client.generate({ prompt, traceId: '...'}); they also accept customHeaders: { 'X-FT-ReqId': '...' }.

5) Structured output / tool-calling
- We support model tool-calling patterns and a JSON-schema enforced structured_output mode. You can register tool metadata (name, input_schema) and the model will return a function_call-style response when appropriate. We can validate outputs and emit a structured_result JSON blob in the response body.

6) Embeddings + reranker recommendation
- Pattern: use embeddings for retrieval (top-K 100) then rerank top-20 with a small LLM prompt that scores each candidate. This gives best precision at modest cost.
- Latency: retrieval from a vector DB (~10-30ms) + reranker (depending on model) ~50-150ms. Cost: reranking small set with a compact model is generally cheaper than scoring all candidates with a large model.

Attachments: redwood-observability-sample-headers.txt (sample header + log field mapping), sdk-snippets.zip (Node/Python examples + tokenization notes)

Related docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/integrations/observability#headers
